description: security:minimumReleaseAgeNpm holds npm updates back until the release is 3 days old. It is here to agree with a gate that already exists downstream: pnpm 12 enforces a 24h minimumReleaseAge at install time (see src/ui/pnpm-workspace.yaml), and a committed lockfile naming a version younger than that fails `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` outright with ERR_PNPM_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE_VIOLATION. With no window configured here, Renovate resolved same-day releases and opened PRs that were red the moment they arrived — #180 landed 15 such entries and needed a re-run hours later rather than any fix. Three days clears the 24h gate with margin, so a PR is installable when it opens.

Renovate's window must stay at or above pnpm's. The package-manager gate is the backstop that also protects developer machines, so the two are layered deliberately and the fix for a red PR is never to lower pnpm's side. internalChecksFilter already defaults to 'strict', so no branch is created while the check is pending — this suppresses the PR, it does not merely annotate it.

Extended as the preset rather than set as a bare minimumReleaseAge because the preset also carves the setting back out (to null) for lockFileMaintenance, bump, lockfileUpdate and rollback — update types Renovate cannot age-check because it is the package manager, not Renovate, that writes those versions. A hand-rolled rule silently skips those carve-outs.

Known gap, so it is not mistaken for a regression: once a PR is already open, a newer release updates that PR immediately and bypasses the window. The cooling-off applies to raising the branch, not to every subsequent push onto it.

packageRules.description: Group non-major updates per ecosystem to keep PR noise low.

Vite majors cannot land alone. vitest carries its own vite as a real dependency, not a peer, so `vitest/config`'s defineConfig types the plugins array against THAT vite — on a mismatch every entry in vite.config.ts fails with 'No overload matches this call' (vite 8 x vitest 3 did exactly this). vite-plugin-svelte is coupled the other way: it peers on one exact vite major, and running it a major behind only degrades `pnpm dev`, which no CI gate covers. Group them so a vite major arrives with the versions that match it. The previous rule here pinned vite-plugin-svelte below 7 while vite was 6; vite 8 landed and made it correct, so grouping replaces the pin.

js-yaml is here only as a pnpm override, to hold orval's copy at or above 4.3.0 for CVE-2026-59869/59870 (see 3d904fe). v5 drops the CommonJS default export, and orval imports it as `import yaml from "js-yaml"` — so v5 breaks `pnpm generate:api` outright while clearing nothing the 4.3 line does not already clear. Revisit when orval ships a v5-compatible import.

TypeScript 7 is installed deliberately as `@typescript/native` (an npm alias for typescript@7), NOT as `typescript`. svelte-check's --tsgo needs BOTH lines present: it runs the Go checker from the alias and still resolves the classic compiler API from `typescript`, which only the 6.x line provides. Bumping this entry to 7 would leave one TypeScript installed instead of two and break `pnpm check`. Hold at 6 until svelte-check can run on 7 alone.
